9
A ball of mass 2.0 kg travels horizontally with a speed of 4.0 m s–1. The ball collides with a wall
and rebounds in the opposite direction with a speed of 2.8 m s–1. The time of the collision is
150 ms.
What is the average force exerted on the wall?
A
16 N
B
37 N
C
53 N
D
91 N

hints: Notice the phrase rebounds in the opposite direction with speeds $4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $2.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and convert the collision time $150 \text{ ms}$ to $0.15 \text{ s}$.
Recall that force is set by change in vector momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, so a direction reversal means the magnitudes add rather than subtract.
Calculate total velocity change as $4.0 + 2.8$, multiply by $2.0 \text{ kg}$ for $\Delta p$, divide by $0.15 \text{ s}$, then use Newton's third law for the force on the wall.
walkthrough: Choose a positive direction, for example towards the wall. Then initial velocity is $+4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and rebound velocity is $-2.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because it is in the opposite direction.
State the impulse rule: average force on the ball is $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$ where $\Delta p = m(v - u)$ and $\Delta t = 150 \text{ ms} = 0.15 \text{ s}$.
Substitute values with units: $\Delta p = 2.0 \times (-2.8 - 4.0) = 2.0 \times (-6.8) = -13.6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Find the magnitude of average force on the ball: $|F| = 13.6 / 0.15 \approx 90.7 \text{ N}$, with unit $\text{kg m s}^{-2} = \text{N}$.
By Newton's third law the wall experiences an equal and opposite force to the ball, so the magnitude on the wall is about $91 \text{ N}$. This is option D

A.explanation: This uses $4.0 - 2.8 = 1.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, which treats speed as a scalar and ignores that rebound in the opposite direction reverses the sign of velocity.

B.explanation: This uses only the rebound momentum $2.0 \times 2.8 / 0.15$, ignoring the initial momentum that must also be reversed.

C.explanation: This uses only the initial momentum $2.0 \times 4.0 / 0.15$, ignoring the additional change needed to send the ball back at $2.8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: This correctly adds the velocity magnitudes for reversal, $2.0 \times (4.0 + 2.8) / 0.15 \approx 91 \text{ N}$.
